note: NWPP KEEPER #3, PROMOTED 2026-09-20 (lane NWPP-44) BY OWNER STANDING RULING, verbatim: "Is this a recommended keeper candidate? If so plz promote. If structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper." THIS PROMOTION IS ON THE HARDER LIMB: a gate DOES regress. C1 fuel-mix goes PASS -> FAIL. The ruling is invoked knowingly, not by reading the easy limb. THE REGRESSION, FIRST AND UNSOFTENED: C1 (LOAD-BEARING) fails on ONE row, 2023 CC_REGULAR, -8.22 TWh / -2.3 pp, volume out of band; 17 of 18 C1 rows pass. It was PREDICTED before any solve -- PRECOMMIT-nwpp-44 §6.2 named CC_REGULAR as the row this arm could push out of band from the other side, because coal displacing gas is the mechanism's intended effect and CC_REGULAR is what absorbs it. Predicted is not the same as harmless: a load-bearing PASS was traded away and that is the price of this keeper. WHY IT IS PROMOTED ANYWAY -- RULE 14 [R-ACCURATE], WHICH GOVERNS THIS EXACT CASE: "If swapping a hand estimate for real data makes the backcast WORSE, that is a signal that something else in the model is miscalibrated and the estimate was silently compensating for it. Treat the worse fit as a discovered bug: KEEP THE ACCURATE INPUT, find and fix the real root cause. Do NOT bury the error back inside an inaccurate input." The arm replaces an ASSUMED uniform 100%-sunk coal first tranche with each plant's MEASURED EIA-923 Schedule-5 contracted share. Reverting to keep C1 green would be exactly the burying rule 14 forbids. The CC_REGULAR gap is therefore ROUTED as the successor's question, not absorbed. THE RUN: NWPP-42's frozen recipe plus EXACTLY TWO armed booleans, both over measured inputs and both carrying ZERO free parameters (rules 21 [R-DOF] / 24 [R-REGISTRY]) -- coal_takeorpay_from_data (each plant's own measured contract share, data/raw/_processed-legacy/coal_takeorpay_NWPP.csv, 13 of 17 plants classified, fleet 94% contract on tonnage) and coal_committed_takeorpay_regulated (the committed-band limb, scoped by the published EIA-860 Regulatory Status == RE). build_dof_ledger emits 4 entries, 3 residual -- the SAME 3 residuals as NWPP-40/41/42; this lane's own entry is measured-physical, so it adds no residual-identified parameter. SCOPE WAS FIXED EX ANTE BY OWNER RULING, AND TO THE HARDER OPTION. On 2026-09-20, on PRECOMMIT-nwpp-43 §7, the owner chose Option B -- ALL regulated coal -- so coal_prb_committed_dispatchable is NOT armed and no rank carve-out is applied. NWPP's own measured conduct does not discriminate between ranks (p25->median CF spread ~9-20 pts in BOTH), and the excluded Option A is the one that would have removed the PRB overshoot risk and pointed the arm at the deficit class. Choosing the carve-out that makes a gate pass is the fitted-mechanism selection rule 1 [R-STRUCT] forbids, so the lane refused to choose it and the owner ruled instead. THE KILL CONDITION WAS PRE-REGISTERED, CARRIED VERBATIM, AND SURVIVED. INERT limb: 2024 COAL_BIT rising < 2.0 TWh => verdict I. It rose +4.898 (7.482 -> 12.381). OVERSHOOT (a): 2024 COAL_BIT > 14.83 => R. It reads 12.381 against an actual 12.832 -- 0.451 UNDER. OVERSHOOT (b): any C1 COAL row out of band => R. Every coal row is inside; C1's single failing row is a GAS row. It was NOT relaxed after the fact: the PRECOMMIT's own zero-LP measurement showed the overshoot limb was out of reach and the INERT limb was the live risk -- the opposite of what NWPP-43 expected -- and the condition was carried unchanged anyway. WHAT IMPROVES. C4 coal, the failure this lane was chartered to close, improves on BOTH metrics in ALL THREE years: r 0.570/0.559/0.524 -> 0.605/0.595/0.610 and NRMSE 0.292/0.387/0.408 -> 0.260/0.246/0.284. NRMSE is now INSIDE the 0.30 gate in all three years where the keeper cleared only 2023. C4 STILL FAILS -- r remains below the 0.70 floor in every year -- and is reported as a FAIL, not a near-miss. Coal volume error against actual (42.27/38.30/42.26 TWh) falls from -0.721/-10.910/-13.943 to +2.028/-1.587/-7.251, i.e. sum|error| 25.574 -> 10.866 TWh, a 57% reduction. THE DISPATCH RESPONSE IS CONFINED TO THE INTENDED SEAM, which is the evidence that this is a mechanism and not an artifact. The offer delta moves 13 LP rows of 641-646, ZERO non-coal rows, |delta pmax| 0.000000 MW, identical in all three years. In dispatch coal displaces gas ONE-FOR-ONE (2025: coal +6.692 TWh against gas -6.694) while hydro, nuclear, wind, solar, biomass and OTHER are unchanged to 0.000 TWh and the system total is conserved to 0.003 TWh. The arm is TWO-SIDED and is not a subsidy: the spot-heavy plants' must-run band gets DEARER (North Valmy $4.50 -> $27.47/MWh on its measured 0.5611 share, out of merit in 6,600 hours of 2024; TS Power $4.50 -> $8.99). WHAT THIS KEEPER DOES NOT CLOSE, STATED AT THE GATE. It does NOT build the rising coal offer curve that NWPP-43 §4.1 diagnosed as the C4 root cause: it ENLARGES the cheap block (_mustrun and _committed collapse to one price at every regulated contracted plant) and leaves the econlo/econhi/peak shelf within $0.51/MWh of itself. If C4 improves it is because coal's volume and gas-price-independence improve, NOT because the stack started rising. The miso-96 objection to discounting the committed band (a take-or-pay contract is an obligation over an accounting period, not a per-hour price) is ANSWERED in PRECOMMIT §3 on the ground that this limb's driver is REGULATORY CONDUCT rather than contract accounting -- but where miso-96 lands (the discounted committed band binds in all 8760 h with no window) is recorded there rather than claimed away. DETERMINATION IS **NOT-YET**, UNCHANGED FROM THE PREDECESSOR, AND THIS KEEPER IS NOT A CALIBRATION. A keeper is the ISO's most structurally faithful registered run (rule 1 [R-STRUCT]), not a claim the market is calibrated. NWPP is additionally PRICE UNSCORED (rubric v3.8, owner card S2): C3a/C3b/C3c are NOT SCORED in any year and this run certifies no price level, shape or tail. GATES: C1 FAIL, C2 PASS, C4 FAIL, C6 PASS, C8 PASS. authorized_price_tuning = NONE -- no offer_curve_by_group band multiplier is touched and this lane never looked at price. NWPP has NO `complete` entry and NO `frontier`, and this promotion deliberately creates neither. HOW IT WAS SOLVED. Three year-isolated shards (rule 36 [R-YEAR-ISOLATION]) pinned to the immutable SHA ee276d873951f4a11b69d3350ac86692b642c006, each pushing its FULL bundle including dispatch/<year>_P1.parquet (rule 34(a)). The parent ran NO LP (rule 32(a)). The registrable bundle was then regenerated through --reuse-solved AT THE LEGS' OWN SOLVE COMMIT at ZERO LP, and verified byte-identical to the legs on every scored quantity (COAL_BIT 18.264/12.381/11.440, hydro 106.872/107.879/113.077). TWO INFRASTRUCTURE DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED EN ROUTE, both affecting EVERY sharded lane, not just this one. (1) A shard's pushed bundle CANNOT be registered on its own: render_calibration_html.build_payload reads the benchmark frames from results/calibration/_shared/<ISO>/, which is gitignored and lives OUTSIDE the bundle dir. (2) A composed span's meta.json carried only the BASE LEG's gas price, which makes plan_reuse_solved refuse every year and forces a full re-solve -- fixed in scripts/probes/_nwpp42_compose_span.py. The NWPP-42 keeper carries that same latent defect (gas_prices {"2023": 2.54} against years [2023,2024,2025]) and is NOT reusable-from until recomposed. Record: docs/FINDING-nwpp44-reuse-solved-cannot-regenerate-shared-2026-09-20.md. CARRIED DEFECTS, ABSORBED NOWHERE. Every NWPP-40/41/42 disclosure is inherited and still applies. Additionally: highspy 1.15.1 in the shard containers against 1.14.0 in the predecessor keeper (unpinnable from this lane; the arm's effects are 1.5-6.7 TWh, far above plausible solver noise, but it is on the record); 2024's P1 ran 11,600 s against its own P0's 1,400 s (8.3x) in the year this arm flips the merit order hardest -- a real observation about the warm-started P1, routed not absorbed; the model-gen vs EIA-930 energy balance is still -10.02 TWh in 2025 against a +/-3.0 tol; C5a CO2 remains a reported-only FAIL. CONTROL for every later NWPP lane = THIS bundle (rule 29(b) form 4); its hourly/ sidecars are committed. LINEAGE: NWPP-40 -> NWPP-41 -> NWPP-42 -> this run. The predecessor is cited by LANE (NWPP-42) rather than by run id, deliberately, because prune_iso_runs.py's citation guard scans this file's text and a run id named here would be PROTECTED from rule 15's keeper-only retention and would later dangle. Records: docs/handoffs/PRECOMMIT-nwpp-44-2026-09-20.md, docs/handoffs/ADDENDUM-nwpp-44-hydro-backfill-2026-09-20.md, docs/handoffs/RESULT-nwpp-44-2026-09-20.md, docs/FINDING-nwpp44-reuse-solved-cannot-regenerate-shared-2026-09-20.md, scripts/gen_nwpp44_attestation.py, scripts/probes/_nwpp44_takeorpay_phase0.py, scripts/probes/_nwpp44_verify_legs.py. *** CORRECTION AND DIAGNOSIS, LANE NWPP-45 (2026-09-22), ZERO LP, NO PROMOTION AND NO MECHANISM ARMED. (a) THE C1 BAND IS +/-8.00 TWh AND THE MISS IS 0.219 TWh. _fuelmix_vol_band is min(max(2% ISO-load, 3% actual-gen), 8 TWh) and THE 8 TWh CAP BINDS for NWPP in every year; the +/-5.41 / +/-5.55 / +/-5.77 quoted in PRECOMMIT-nwpp-44 section 6.1 and carried into the matrix stamp is wrong. 2023 CC_REGULAR reads 47.996 against 56.215, so the VOLUME leg misses by 0.219 TWh -- 2.7% of the band -- and the SHARE leg (-2.32 pp against +/-3.0 pp) is INSIDE. 2024 CC_REGULAR PASSES at -6.323; every 2025 row is SKIPPED on the preliminary EIA-923 vintage. This does not make the regression harmless and is not a reason to relax anything; it changes what the defect IS. (b) IT IS NOT A CC_REGULAR DEFECT. Measured on this keeper's own committed hourly/ sidecars and a fleet_only=True rebuild on its own recipe: the shortfall is UNIFORM across every load quintile (-1.6 to -2.7 TWh each, ~-900 to -1,400 MW in every hour of 2023), so it is neither commitment nor offer-level; the class carries ~30 TWh of UNUSED ENVELOPE (78.347 TWh availability-weighted against 47.996 dispatched), so it is not capacity or availability; and EVERY ZONE is short of nearly every family in every year with NONE over-generating, so it is not coal displacing gas locally. It is a SYSTEM ENERGY-REQUIREMENT GAP of -9.645 / -12.144 / -9.107 TWh that the marginal class absorbs because every non-thermal class is separately pinned to a measured budget (non-thermal is within 0.056 / 0.057 TWh of actual in 2023 / 2024). (c) THE IDENTITY, CLOSING TO 0.049 / 0.059 / 0.107 TWh IN ALL THREE YEARS. The LP's demand is EIA-930 pool Net generation (Adj) LESS GRID's Desert-Southwest interchange legs (7.115 / 9.774 / 10.131 TWh) -- B - C reproduces the demand array to the milli-TWh -- while C1 scores against the EIA-923 plant basis (classFull 280.154 / 289.852 / 297.913). The two sources disagree by 21.3 TWh over an IDENTICAL plant set: all 881 footprint plants carry a BACODE in NWPP_BAS and zero pool-BA plants are missing, so this is a SOURCE disagreement, not a boundary error. The largest terms are GRID +12.856 (its EIA-930 BA reports 16.774 TWh of net generation including 4.143 TWh of COAL, while eGRID assigns exactly ONE plant to BACODE GRID -- 55328 Hermiston, a gas CC, 3.918 TWh) and BPAT -15.169 -- the signature of generation-only balancing authorities. (d) THE OBVIOUS FIX IS REFUTED BEFORE ANY LP. Applying the construction's own stated principle literally -- subtract GRID's out-of-footprint GENERATION (12.856 TWh) rather than its Southwest LEGS (7.115) -- lowers demand a further 5.741 TWh and makes C1 WORSE; zeroing the subtraction is the over-ask it exists to prevent. (e) NOTHING WAS ARMED, NOTHING SOLVED, NO KEEPER MOVED. The remedy is a demand-construction change worth 9-12 TWh/yr that moves every class in every NWPP year, and rule 1 [R-STRUCT] forbids this lane selecting it because the residual is exactly what would be moving. It is put to the owner as a scope question with three framings and the LP cost of validating any of them. What must NOT happen is closing 0.219 TWh by weakening NWPP-44's take-or-pay arm: that is the burying rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] forbids and it would leave 9.6 TWh untouched underneath. ALSO RE-SCORED AND UNCHANGED: C4 coal still FAILS in all three years (r 0.605 / 0.595 / 0.610 against a 0.70 floor; NRMSE 0.260 / 0.246 / 0.284, inside 0.30 everywhere), root cause still the rising-curve defect. ALSO NOTED: the 2025 energy balance of -10.02 TWh against a +/-3.0 tol is the SAME object as the C1 gap, measured on the EIA-930 leg instead of the EIA-923 leg.
